graphEvents.label: changed-docs module imported only on zero-hit

label: Module boundary is a new lib/changed-docs.mjs imported dynamically inside the zero-hit branch, so a lookup hit pays no extra module load.
lookup() stays synchronous and unchanged; a new exported async lookupWithFallback() calls it with limit 0, merges fallback rows and re-slices, and main() becomes async.

Candidate source is git status --porcelain=v1 -z --untracked-files=all -- <roots>; -z removes quoting and rename ambiguity, and --untracked-files=all prevents a wholly untracked packet directory collapsing to one entry.

Porcelain parsing keeps staged additions, consumes the second NUL field for renames and copies keeping the new path, skips deletions, and excludes directories and submodules via the .md suffix plus isFile().

The fallback root comes from callerRepoRoot(), --spec-folder becomes the git pathspec, and an explicit --index disables the fallback, which keeps fixtures hermetic and resolves the determinism tension.

Scoring reads declared trigger_phrases with readTriggerPhrases, scores each normalized phrase with scorePhrase, keeps the best per document with the matchClassRank tie-break, and sorts candidate paths with compareCodeUnits before reading.
The answer gains staleFallback {available, files, matches, paths, truncated} only when the fallback ran, appended last so the common-path JSON stays byte-identical.
Exit 0 when any merged result scores above zero, exit 1 only when index and fallback both produce nothing, exit 2 unchanged.
Opt-out is --no-stale-fallback, with the implicit --index opt-out covering parity fixtures and determinism tests.

Performance budget: scoped git 0.02-0.03s plus frontmatter 0.02s against a 0.07s lookup, repo-wide 0.88-0.90s about 13x, bounded by zero-hit-only execution and MAX_FALLBACK_FILES 200 over the sorted candidate list.

Compatibility is clean on the production side: generate-trigger-index.mjs and core/workflow.ts import only loadIndex, no production caller parses the answer, and test assertions are field-level rather than whole-object.
Contract text is two blocks: a section 4 keyed-lane zero-hit fallback note after the exit table, and a section 5 determinism-scope paragraph replacing the unchanged-corpus promise at line 212.

The test matrix is 18 cases: staged addition, untracked directory, rename, deletion, non-git, missing git binary, explicit-index isolation, opt-out, dedup, scope, limit, cap, determinism, empty tokens, both formats and the existing lookup blocks.
lookup() remains synchronous and its return shape is unchanged.
The fallback runs only on a zero-hit, only inside a git work tree, and only when the index path was not passed explicitly.
The keyed lane never produces a result from body text; only declared trigger_phrases are scored.

reason: The keyed lane matches declared phrases, not prose; prose belongs to the ripgrep lane.
Measured loss of 14 of 29 changed docs, all staged additions.

direction: mtime comparison or a pending-reindex queue
reason: The index has no publish timestamp and checkout mtimes are not build times.
It is a full corpus walk and by contract never runs per lookup.

direction: making lookup() async or embedding fallback logic in it
reason: Would break the exported synchronous contract the test suite asserts.

direction: enabling the fallback for an explicit --index
reason: Would make temp-corpus fixtures depend on the developer's worktree.
